title: Rail adapter fork + comparator copies
note: Core confirmed: Rail.tsx loadedSection (:628-646), projectsFor (:827-846), projectFromSummary (:655-697, mode 'compatibility', compatibilityError cache key) keep a non-normalized path; store.ts:503-534 sets normalized for every decoded snapshot/delta/gone and revalidator.ts:335-340 carries it through, so production resources with data always have normalized. Rail.tsx is 2133 lines, Rail.test.tsx 3617. Overstated: loadedSection returns RailSession via selectRailModel, a richer type than the shared selectors' NavigationSessionSummary rows, so it does not simply 're-derive' selectLiveRows. The ten comparators are not all the same (Rail.tsx:549-556 sorts project pages by tier/offset/limit/keyID; :893 sorts by pin_catalog offset only). adaptNavigationResources (Rail.tsx:948) is not 'exported only for a test': Rail.test.tsx calls it ~10 times (:905,:933,:1017,:1126...) as the adapter seam, so it cannot be dropped independently. Severity medium: dead compat branch plus test-reseeding cost, no live drift evidenced.
revised_fix_plan: 1) Make Rail.test.tsx resource() seeding build normalized (normalizedResource helper at :168 already exists), then delete the non-normalized branches, projectFromSummary, mode discriminator and compatibilityError. 2) Add a shared pagesInOrder only for the genuinely identical offset/limit sorts (selectors.ts:113,129,166; needsYouActions.ts:51,387; Rail.tsx:621,893); leave the project-page tier sort alone. 3) Keep adaptNavigationResources exported (tests use it) or move the adapter to stores/navigation/railResources.ts together with its tests. 4) Update docs/product/subsystems.md rail row.

Replace round citations with invariants.

title: requireClass boilerplate
note: Counts reproduced: ~1306 requireClass(styles.*) call sites in 194 non-test files repo-wide (finding's 1,297; slice-only is 497 in 82 files). But the premise 'typing-only' is wrong: requireClass throws at module load in the real build (requireClass.ts:15-21), and styles/requireclass-contract.test.ts (397 lines) exists because vitest leaves CSS Modules unprocessed, so the runtime guard is blind in tests; the contract test statically verifies every referenced class exists in the real stylesheet. Replacing it is a ~1,300-site codemod and a convention documented as 'canonical pattern for every widget'. A real design question for Jesse, low value for the churn.
revised_fix_plan: Raise with Jesse only if he wants it; simplest option is a single ambient module typing or one cssClasses(styles, names) per module. Not a debt PR on its own.
